title: Walking Robot Simulation II
statement:
A grid has `width` columns and `height` rows. Cell `(x, y)` uses `x` for the column and `y` for the row, with `(0, 0)` in the bottom-left corner and `(width - 1, height - 1)` in the top-right. A robot starts on `(0, 0)` facing `"East"`. Implement the `Robot` class:

- `Robot(width, height)` sets up the grid and places the robot as described.
- `step(num)` makes the robot take `num` single moves, one after another. For each move, if the cell directly ahead is on the grid, the robot goes there. Otherwise it rotates 90 degrees counterclockwise (East to North, North to West, West to South, South to East) and tries the same move again. It only turns when blocked, so after stopping it still faces the way it last moved.
- `getPos()` returns the robot's cell as `[x, y]`.
- `getDir()` returns the direction it faces: `"North"`, `"East"`, `"South"` or `"West"`.
constraints: At most 10^4 calls are made to step, getPos and getDir in total
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating every single move is too slow: `num` can be 10^5 and there can be 10^4 calls. But the robot starts on the border, and a border robot that hits a wall turns along the next side, so it never leaves the border. Its path is one loop of length `2 * (width - 1) + 2 * (height - 1)`, so the only state that matters is how far along the loop it is, taken modulo the loop length. The direction then follows from which side of the loop it stands on.

## Approach

1. Store `right = width - 1`, `top = height - 1` and `perimeter = 2 * (right + top)`. Start with `index = 0` and `moved = false`.
2. `step(num)`: set `moved` and advance `index` by `num`, modulo `perimeter`.
3. `locate()` turns `index` into a cell and direction by walking the four sides in order: bottom (East), right side (North), top (West), left side (South). Each side's end corner belongs to that side, because the robot arrives there still facing that way.
4. Index 0 is the start corner: the robot faces East if it has never moved, and South if it came back around the loop.
5. `getPos()` and `getDir()` read the parts they need from `locate()`.

## Example 1, step by step

Width 6 and height 3 give `right = 5`, `top = 2`, `perimeter = 14`. Two `step(2)` calls bring `index` to 4, which is on the bottom side: `[4, 0]`, `"East"`. Then `step(2)` makes it 6, `step(1)` makes it 7, and `step(4)` makes it 11. Since `7 < 11 <= 12`, the robot is on the top side at `x = 5 - (11 - 5 - 2) = 1`: `[1, 2]`, `"West"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1) per call: one addition and modulo, or a few comparisons.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- The start cell is ambiguous: before any move the robot faces East, but after looping back it faces South.
- A corner belongs to the side the robot arrived on (`[right, 0]` is East, not North): it only turns when the next move is blocked.
- Reducing `num` modulo `perimeter` alone is not enough; keep the `moved` flag so `step(perimeter)` still reports South.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `right`, `top` | largest `x` and `y` on the grid |
| `perimeter` | number of moves to go once around the border |
| `index` | distance travelled along the border, modulo `perimeter` |
| `moved` | whether `step` has ever been called |
| `x`, `y` | the cell returned by `getPos` |

narration.3: The largest x on the grid, the bottom-right corner's column.
narration.4: The largest y on the grid, the top row.
narration.5: Going once around the border takes this many moves.
narration.7: Remember whether the robot has moved, to tell the two meanings of the start cell apart.
narration.12: The robot only ever travels around the border, so only its place on that loop matters.
narration.17: Back at the start corner: it faces East before moving, South after coming around.
narration.18: On the bottom side, travelling East.
narration.19: On the right side, travelling North.
narration.20: On the top side, travelling West.
narration.21: Otherwise it is on the left side, travelling South.
narration.25: Take the cell part of the located state.
narration.30: Take the direction part of the located state.
